overview:
Auli sits in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district and is India's best-known skiing destination, with wide open slopes and big panoramic views of the Himalayas, including Nanda Devi. The meadows sit at roughly 2,500m to 3,050m, skiing season runs from January to March, and the famous cable car makes it a popular hill station all year round.

This is a **2 Nights / 3 Days** group trip with transfers in an AC traveller or bus on the Delhi, Govindghat, Joshimath, Delhi route. Day 1 is the drive to Govindghat, where you stay both nights in a hotel. Day 2 is the big one: a day visit to Auli for snow fun and skiing, plus the trek to Gorson Bugyal, the beautiful high meadow above Auli. You can also check out Auli Artificial Lake and end the evening around a bonfire. Day 3 is departure.

You get 2 breakfasts and 2 dinners, a Trip Coordinator with you throughout, and 24x7 customer support. Just note that the ropeway (cable car or chair car) to Auli is not included, so keep some budget aside if you want to ride it.

faqs.q: How long is the Auli trip?
faqs.a: It is a 2 Nights / 3 Days trip. Both nights are spent in a hotel at Govindghat, with a day visit to Auli and the Gorson Bugyal trek in between.

faqs.q: What is included in the Auli package?
faqs.a: AC traveller or bus transfers on the Delhi, Govindghat, Joshimath, Delhi route, two nights in a hotel at Govindghat, 2 breakfasts and 2 dinners, a day visit to Auli with the Gorson Bugyal trek, a Trip Coordinator throughout, and 24x7 customer support.

faqs.q: Is the Auli cable car ride included?
faqs.a: No. The ropeway (cable car or chair car) to Auli is excluded, along with any meals beyond the package inclusions and any entry tickets to monuments and public places.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start?
faqs.a: Transfers run from Delhi and back to Delhi. Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: When can I see snow and ski in Auli?
faqs.a: Auli's skiing season is roughly January to March, which is when you are most likely to find snow on the slopes. The rest of the year it is a green hill station with great Himalayan views.

faqs.q: How much does the Auli trip cost?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹7,999 per person on Triple Sharing, and Dual Sharing is ₹8,499 per person. Prices can change, so check the latest price on this page.

faqs.q: When are the departures?
faqs.a: We run departures every Friday; see Upcoming departures on this page for dates.

faqs.q: Can I join the Auli trip solo?
faqs.a: Yes, many travellers join solo. Groups are usually 8 to 50 people, so it is an easy way to meet fellow travellers.

overview:
Chakrata is an old British Indian Army cantonment town in Dehradun district, Uttarakhand, tucked between the Tons and Yamuna rivers at an elevation of 2,118m, about 98 km from Dehradun. Quiet forests, fresh mountain air and some seriously good viewpoints make it a perfect quick escape.

This **1 Night / 2 Days** weekend getaway covers all travel and transfers in an AC traveller or bus. Day 1 you reach Chakrata and head out on the trek to Budher Caves, then settle into your resort for an evening of bonfire and music. Day 2 is for Tiger Falls, one of the region's best-known waterfalls, and the views from Chirmiri Neck Top before heading back. Other highlights on the trip include Moila Top and a stroll around Chakrata Market.

You get 1 night in a resort at Chakrata, 1 breakfast, 1 dinner and evening snacks, a Trip Coordinator throughout the trip, and 24x7 customer support. Short, fun and easy to fit into a weekend.

faqs.q: How long is the Chakrata trip?
faqs.a: It is a 1 Night / 2 Days weekend trip, with one night's stay in a resort at Chakrata.

faqs.q: What is included?
faqs.a: All travel and transfers in an AC traveller or bus, 1 night in a resort at Chakrata, 1 breakfast, 1 dinner and evening snacks, the Budher Caves trek, a visit to Chirmiri Neck Top and Tiger Falls, bonfire and music, a Trip Coordinator throughout, and 24x7 customer support.

faqs.q: What is not included?
faqs.a: Meals beyond the package inclusions, entry tickets to monuments and public places, photo or video charges during paragliding, and any expense not listed in the inclusions. Extra costs from natural calamities or other situations beyond control are also excluded.

faqs.q: What will we see on the trip?
faqs.a: Day 1 is the trek to Budher Caves after reaching Chakrata, and Day 2 covers Tiger Falls and Chirmiri Neck Top. Moila Top, Chakrata Market and a DJ and bonfire night are also among the trip highlights.

faqs.a: Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: How much does the Chakrata trip cost?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹4,499 per person on Quad Sharing. Triple Sharing is ₹4,699 and Dual Sharing is ₹4,899 per person. Prices can change, so check the latest on this page.

faqs.q: When are the departures?

faqs.a: Yes, many travellers join solo. Groups are usually 8 to 50 people.

overview:
Chopta is a peaceful high-altitude meadow in Uttarakhand, often called the "Mini Switzerland of India". It is the base for the trek to Tungnath, the world's highest Shiva temple at 3,680m, and further up to the Chandrashila summit at 3,960m. It is a year-round trekking favourite: come between April and June for lush green meadows, or January to March for snow.

This **2 Nights / 3 Days** trip runs Delhi to Delhi by tempo traveller or cab. Day 1 takes you past the Devprayag Sangam and on to Chopta. Day 2 is adventure and sightseeing, with the Tungnath Temple and Chandrashila trek as the headline act. On Day 3 you drive to Sari Village and trek to Deoriatal, a lovely lake known for its mountain reflections, before heading home.

You stay 2 nights in Swiss camps or a homestay, with veg meals (2 dinners, 2 breakfasts and 2 evening snacks, from Day 1 evening snacks to Day 3 breakfast). An experienced Trip Captain and trek guide leads the way, a bonfire is on when the weather permits, and driver allowances, tolls, parking and state taxes are covered, plus 24x7 customer support.

faqs.q: How long is the Chopta Tungnath trip?
faqs.a: It is a 2 Nights / 3 Days trip, with both nights in Swiss camps or a homestay.

faqs.q: What is included?
faqs.a: Delhi to Delhi transport by tempo traveller or cab, 2 nights in Swiss camps or a homestay, a Trip Captain and trek guide, bonfire (if weather permits), local explorations as per the itinerary, veg meals (2 dinners, 2 breakfasts, 2 evening snacks), driver allowances, toll taxes, parking, state taxes, and 24x7 customer support.

faqs.q: What is not included?
faqs.a: Any meals or food beyond the package inclusions and any entry tickets to monuments and public places.

faqs.q: Which treks does the trip cover?
faqs.a: The trip covers the trek to Tungnath Temple and Chandrashila, and on Day 3 the trek to Deoriatal from Sari Village.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start?
faqs.a: The trip runs Delhi to Delhi. Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: What is the best time to go?
faqs.a: April to June is great for green meadows, and January to March is when you are likely to find snow. Tungnath sits at 3,680m and Chandrashila at 3,960m, so carry warm layers in any season.

faqs.q: How much does it cost?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹5,799 per person on Quad Sharing. Triple Sharing is ₹6,199 and Dual Sharing is ₹6,399 per person. Prices can change, so check the latest on this page.

faqs.a: We run departures every Friday; see Upcoming departures on this page for dates. Many travellers join solo, and groups are usually 8 to 50 people.

overview:
Goa is India's smallest state by area and one of its favourite escapes, loved for its beaches, nightlife and Portuguese heritage. More than 450 years as a Portuguese colony shows in its churches, food and easy-going vibe, including the UNESCO World Heritage churches of Old Goa like the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral. The coastline has something for every mood, from lively Baga, Calangute and Anjuna to calmer Palolem, Agonda and Morjim.

This **4 Nights / 5 Days** backpacking trip is a road trip in AC vehicles from Pune, Bangalore or Hyderabad. Once you arrive, it is "Goa with strangers" who quickly become friends, then an offbeat plus market day, a "not so offbeat" day, and a run down South before your last moments by the sea. Along the way you hike to Cabo de Rama beach, go kayaking, watch the sunset at Dona Paula, hike to the lake at Arambol beach for a dip and some local market shopping, and have the option of a casino or Tito's Lane evening (entry at your own cost).

You stay 4 nights in a 3 to 4 star resort with a pool party, and get 4 breakfasts, 1 lunch and 1 dinner, local sightseeing, all internal travel within Goa with fuel and driver, Trip Captains, and 24x7 travel assistance.

faqs.q: How long is the Goa backpacking trip?
faqs.a: It is a 4 Nights / 5 Days trip with 4 nights in a 3 to 4 star resort, plus the road journey to Goa.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start from?
faqs.a: The trip includes a road trip in AC vehicles from Pune, Bangalore or Hyderabad. Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: What is included?
faqs.a: The road trip in AC vehicles, 4 nights in a 3 to 4 star resort, 4 breakfasts, 1 lunch and 1 dinner, Trip Captains, local sightseeing, all internal travel within Goa with fuel and driver, a pool party at the hotel, and 24x7 travel assistance.

faqs.q: What is not included?
faqs.a: Meals not mentioned in the itinerary, casino entry, club entry and the food, drinks and GST at clubs, alcoholic beverages, and any expenses caused by unforeseen circumstances.

faqs.q: What will we do in Goa?
faqs.a: Highlights include a small hike to Cabo de Rama beach, kayaking, sunset at Dona Paula, a hike to the lake at Arambol beach with a dip and local market shopping, a day in South Goa, and an optional casino or Tito's Lane night (entry fees excluded).

faqs.q: How much does the Goa trip cost?
faqs.a: It starts from ₹11,499 per person on Dual Sharing, and Triple Sharing is ₹12,999 per person. Prices can change, so check the latest on this page.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Goa?
faqs.a: November to February is peak season with pleasant, dry weather. The monsoon, roughly June to September, is green and quieter but the sea is rough.

faqs.q: When are the departures, and can I join solo?
faqs.a: We run departures every Friday; see Upcoming departures on this page for dates. Yes, many travellers join solo, and groups are usually 8 to 50 people.

overview:
Jaisalmer, the "Golden City" of Rajasthan, is a magical mix of history and desert adventure, best visited between October and March. At its heart is the 12th-century Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila), a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the few living forts in the world, surrounded by ornately carved havelis and golden sandstone lanes.

This **2 Nights / 3 Days** group trip covers all travel as per the itinerary in a tempo traveller or mini bus. Day 1 you reach Jaisalmer and set off on a city tour: think the fort, Patwon-ki-Haveli, Nathmal-ki-Haveli, Salim Singh-ki-Haveli and an easy evening at Gadisar Lake. Day 2 takes you to the Longewala battlefield, with offbeat stops like Kuldhara abandoned village, Bada Bagh cenotaphs and the War Museum among the trip highlights. Out at the Sam Sand Dunes you get jeep dune bashing, a camel safari and that famous desert sunset, followed by a night in Swiss tents with a bonfire and Rajasthani folk music and dance. Day 3 wraps up the city tour before departure.

You stay 2 nights on a sharing basis in a hotel and Swiss tents, with 4 meals (2 breakfasts, 2 dinners), local sightseeing, an experienced trip leader, 24x7 onboard assistance, and driver allowances, tolls, parking and state taxes covered.

faqs.q: How long is the Jaisalmer trip?
faqs.a: It is a 2 Nights / 3 Days trip, with stays on a sharing basis in a hotel and in Swiss tents.

faqs.q: What is included?
faqs.a: All travel as per the itinerary in a tempo traveller or mini bus, 2 nights in a hotel and Swiss tents, 4 meals (2 breakfasts, 2 dinners), local sightseeing, jeep dune bashing and a camel safari, a trip leader, 24x7 onboard assistance, and driver allowances, tolls, parking and state taxes.

faqs.q: What is not included?
faqs.a: Alcoholic beverages, personal and medical expenses, and anything not listed in the inclusions. Costs from road blockages, accidents, landslides or itinerary changes beyond our control are borne by the traveller on the spot.

faqs.q: Are the desert safari and camp included?
faqs.a: Yes. Jeep dune bashing and a camel safari are included, and one of the two nights is in Swiss tents with a bonfire and Rajasthani folk music and dance.

faqs.q: What does the itinerary cover?
faqs.a: Day 1 is arrival and a Jaisalmer city tour, Day 2 is the Longewala battlefield, and Day 3 is a city tour before departure. Highlights include Jaisalmer Fort, the havelis, Gadisar Lake, Sam Sand Dunes, Kuldhara, Bada Bagh and the War Museum.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start?
faqs.a: Your exact reporting point and time are shared after booking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Jaisalmer?
faqs.a: October to March, when desert days are pleasant. Nights in the desert can get cold in winter, so pack a warm layer.
